papers.title: [MOCK] Lightweight CNNs for Leaf Disease Classification on Mobile Devices
papers.abstract: We study compact convolutional networks for classifying leaf diseases from smartphone photos. A MobileNet-style model trained on PlantVillage reaches 97.2% accuracy while running at 30 ms per image on a mid-range phone.

papers.title: [MOCK] Vision Transformers for Plant Pathology in Uncontrolled Field Conditions
papers.abstract: Most plant disease datasets are captured in the lab. We collect 12,000 field images across five crops and show that a ViT-B/16 pretrained on ImageNet-21k achieves 88.4% top-1 accuracy, outperforming ResNet-50 by 6 points.

papers.title: [MOCK] Domain Shift in Leaf Disease Recognition: From PlantVillage to the Field
papers.abstract: Models trained on lab images often fail in the field. We measure accuracy drops of up to 40 points when transferring PlantVillage models to field photos and evaluate data augmentation and test-time adaptation as mitigations.

papers.title: [MOCK] Few-Shot Detection of Emerging Crop Diseases with Prototypical Networks
papers.abstract: New diseases appear with few labelled examples. We apply prototypical networks to five-shot classification of rare tomato and cassava diseases, reaching 81% accuracy on real field photos.

papers.title: [MOCK] Multispectral Drone Imagery for Early Wheat Rust Detection
papers.abstract: We combine multispectral UAV imagery with a U-Net segmentation model to detect wheat yellow rust before visible symptoms appear, achieving an F1 score of 0.86 on a three-season dataset.

papers.title: [MOCK] Explainable Attention Maps for Trustworthy Plant Disease Diagnosis
papers.abstract: We evaluate Grad-CAM and attention rollout explanations for plant disease classifiers and run a user study with 24 agronomists, finding that explanations increased trust but rarely changed decisions.

review_md:
## Overview
Deep learning has become the dominant approach to automated crop disease detection, moving from lab-captured leaf images towards real field conditions [1][2][3].

## Key Themes
**Efficiency for deployment.** Lightweight CNNs make on-device diagnosis practical, reaching 97.2% accuracy at 30 ms per image on a phone [1].

**Robustness to field conditions.** Vision transformers outperform CNNs on uncontrolled field images [2], while models trained on PlantVillage can lose up to 40 accuracy points in the field [3].

**Data scarcity.** Few-shot learning offers a route to recognising emerging diseases from only five examples per class [4].

**Beyond RGB.** Multispectral drone imagery enables detection before symptoms are visible [5].

## Methods & Results Comparison
| Ref | Method | Data | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1] | Lightweight CNN | PlantVillage | 97.2% acc. |
| [2] | ViT-B/16 | Field images | 88.4% top-1 |
| [4] | Prototypical nets | Field photos | 81% (5-shot) |
| [5] | U-Net + multispectral | UAV | F1 0.86 |

## Research Gaps
High lab accuracy does not transfer reliably to the field [3], and most field studies cover only a handful of crops [2][4]. Explainability improves trust among agronomists but has little effect on their decisions, which suggests explanations are not yet actionable [6].

## Conclusion
The field is shifting from lab benchmarks to robust, efficient and data-efficient models suited to real farms [1][2][4].
